# AstorNova: The Dream Journey
**Space Mission Design Game – Project Summary**

AstorNova is an educational space mission design game that allows players to experience the role of a space engineer. Players select missions, design rockets, choose components, and manage limited resources such as fuel, energy, weight, and budget.

Guided by Neva, an AI-powered assistant, players receive real-time feedback, warnings, and suggestions to improve their designs and decisions.

The game features progressive missions, starting with Earth orbit, throw the odessy all the way leading to a final challenge involving a mysterious signal near Jupiter . Players must design a suitable spacecraft within specific time and budget limits.

AstorNova aims to make space engineering more engaging while developing problem-solving, critical thinking, and decision-making skills through interactive learning and realistic challenges.
details:
AstorNova: The Dream Journey is an interactive, educational space mission design game where players step into the role of a space engineer.

1.
Core Gameplay Loop: Players select a mission, assemble a spacecraft by choosing specific components (engines, fuel tanks, shields, sensors, etc.), and balance five critical constraints: Fuel, Energy, Weight, Budget, and Time.

Progressive Missions: The journey begins in Earth Orbit to teach core mechanics, advances through increasingly complex deep-space missions, and culminates in a final expedition to investigate a mysterious signal near Jupiter.

AI Guidance (Neva): Throughout the design and flight phases, players are assisted by Neva, an AI-powered mission assistant that analyzes spacecraft configurations in real time, flags critical HUD warnings (such as weight overloads or budget deficits), and offers optimization suggestions.

Dynamic Outcomes: Based on engineering choices and resource management, every mission concludes with one of three outcomes: Mission Failed, Partial Success, or Perfect Success.

2.

  • Hands-On STEM Learning: Translates complex aerospace and resource-management concepts into an intuitive, trial-and-error interactive environment.
  • Risk-Free Experimentation: Allows learners to test engineering trade-offs (e.g., adding heavier armor vs. conserving fuel and budget) and immediately see the consequences without real-world costs.
  • Personalized Real-Time Mentorship: With Neva acting as an intelligent tutor, players aren't left guessing why a design failed; they receive targeted, actionable feedback to improve their engineering logic.

3.

The project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical space science and engaging interactive media. By gamifying spacecraft engineering, AstorNova seeks to:

  • Inspire students and aspiring innovators to explore aerospace engineering and space exploration.
  • Cultivate transferable cognitive skills—specifically problem-solving, critical thinking, and strategic decision-making under strict constraints.
  • Make space mission design accessible to anyone with a web browser, turning passive learners into active mission architects.

4.

  • Development & AI Platforms: Built and deployed as a web application via Google AI Studio (astornova-the-dream-journey.ai.studio), utilizing Gemini for AI workflow integration, code generation, and powering the logic behind Neva.
  • Web Technologies & Languages: Developed using standard modern web architecture (HTML, CSS, JavaScript / TypeScript, and React) to create interactive UI overlays, mission HUDs, and real-time resource calculators.
  • Design & Asset Creation: Used AI image-generation tools and digital illustration workflows to create custom sci-fi UI icons, spacecraft components, planetary visuals, and mission badges, alongside presentation/documentation tools for project planning.
  • Hardware: Developed and tested on personal laptops (such as Windows-based systems) with standard web browsers for cross-device compatibility.

5.

  • Narrative-Driven Engineering: Instead of a dry physics calculator, the game weaves engineering constraints into a cohesive sci-fi narrative—an odyssey from Earth to a mysterious signal at Jupiter.
  • AI Co-Pilot Integration: Embedding Neva directly into the gameplay loop transforms standard error messages into an interactive dialogue with an intelligent mission companion.
  • Turning Constraints into Creative Design: Faced with 3D rendering complexity, storage limits, and strict AI usage quotas, the team creatively pivoted to a sleek, stylized 2D/isometric sci-fi interface with optimized visual assets—delivering a rich, responsive experience without sacrificing depth.

6.

Our team (Fatima Ali, Naba Mirza, Batool S. Saeed, and Fatima Mohammed) factored in both educational game design and technical feasibility:


Balance & Realism vs. Accessibility: Ensuring the trade-offs between weight, fuel, energy, time, and budget feel authentic to real space missions while remaining intuitive for beginners.

Technical & Resource Constraints: Managing AI quota limits, browser storage restrictions, and tight development timelines by prioritizing core gameplay mechanics and optimizing asset sizes.

User Experience (UX) & Clarity: Designing clean HUD indicators, clear tutorial steps, and immediate visual/textual warnings so players always understand why a spacecraft succeeds or fails.
